thumbnails.concept_ko: 한 줄: "인도 공장에서 중국 기술자가 통째로 빠져나갔다." verified-data 2절 — 2025년 7·8월 두 차례에 걸쳐 폭스콘 인도 공장의 중국인 엔지니어 300여 명이 철수했고, 그 자리를 대만 인력이 메웠다. 유리 한 장을 경계로 밖은 흐르고(빠져나가는 행렬) 안은 멈춰 있어(빈 작업대) 모순이 한 화면에 들어온다. 메시지 6채널: ①등을 보인 이탈 방향 ④Foxconn 로고 ⑤류양웨이의 낭패 ⑥벗어 두고 간 파란 방진모와 흰 목장갑.
thumbnails.prompt_en: A candid photograph taken inside the main gate hall of the Foxconn iPhone assembly plant in Chennai, India, looking out through the full-height glass onto the yard. COMPOSITION RULE, HIGHEST PRIORITY: the photograph fills the entire 16:9 frame edge to edge with a real scene — never a letterbox band, never an empty panel, never a flat colour block, and never a large expanse of bare empty floor. The bottom three-eighths of the frame height is filled by the dark backs and shoulders of the people nearest the camera, so far out of focus and so deeply in shadow that it reads as one single dark mass with no readable detail, which keeps overlay text legible on top of it. No face, no hand, no sign and no bright object sits in that bottom three-eighths — every face, hand, sign and key object sits in the upper five-eighths. Work benches and counters run across the MIDDLE of the frame, never near the bottom edge, and anything resting on them sits at mid height. SCALE, EQUALLY IMPORTANT: Young Liu, chairman of Foxconn, is the largest thing in the picture — his head and shoulders occupy the entire right third of the frame, his face alone spans roughly the top 55 to 60 percent of the frame height, the top of his hair touches the upper edge and is very slightly cropped by it, and his shoulder leaves the frame on the right. The other people are far smaller, roughly one third of his head height. Camera at standing eye level, frontal. Beyond the glass a long column of Chinese engineers in plain dark jackets walks away from the camera towards the gate, every one of them with his back turned, wheeling cabin suitcases and carrying grey canvas tool bags; that column is slightly motion-blurred while the interior stays perfectly still. Inside, the hall has stopped: an empty steel work bench crosses the middle of the frame with a pale blue dust cap and one white cotton glove left on it, a wall board behind it carries the Foxconn logo, and cool fluorescent tubes overhead mix with flat overcast Indian daylight coming through the glass. Young Liu stands on the right, chest up — his eyelids hang half closed, his gaze unfocused and trailing the tail of the column, his lower lip rolled inward and bitten, his nostrils flared, and the back of one hand is pressed to his forehead and dragging slowly across it. Style: candid documentary photograph of a real place, not an advertisement, not CGI, not a composite. Shot on a full-frame camera with a 35mm lens at about f/2.8, standing eye level, available light only, true-to-life restrained colour, mild sensor noise, a slight handheld tilt, honest texture on skin, glass, steel and concrete. Signs may clip a little but the overall image stays natural — never glowing, never hyper-saturated, no HDR look, no rim-light effects, no lens flare. Apart from the Foxconn logo named above, do not invent any other Korean, Chinese or English words or letterforms anywhere in the image. No title overlay text, no captions, no subtitle bars, no large lettering across the frame, no watermark.

thumbnails.concept_ko: 확정 제목 3단 「일대일로가 남긴 빚더미」의 착지 장면. verified-data 5절 — 마탈라 라자팍사 국제공항은 1단계 사업비 2억 900만 달러 중 1억 9,000만 달러가 중국수출입은행 돈이었고, 개항 뒤 전기요금조차 못 대는 적자에 포브스가 '세계에서 가장 텅 빈 국제공항'이라 명명했다. 이 자리에 세울 진영 대표 얼굴이 없으므로 규칙대로 사람을 빼고 현장으로 화면을 세웠다(무명 민간인 금지). 6채널: ①활주로를 갈라 나온 잡초의 선 ②빛이 꺼진 무채색 ④터미널 외벽의 공항 이름 ⑥먼지 앉은 체크인 카운터와 꺼진 전광판.

Not one aircraft is anywhere in the picture. Tall grass and weeds push up through every expansion joint of the runway and along the taxiway edge, and a low scrub line has crept onto the apron itself. The long glass terminal has all its lights switched off; through the glass, check-in counters stand under a film of dust with their conveyor belts bare, the flight display boards are blank and dark, and a folded wheelchair leans against a pillar. Above the terminal entrance raised metal letters read "MATTALA". A single rusted set of boarding stairs stands parked and unused. Heavy monsoon-grey sky, flat diffuse light, no sun, no shadows sharp enough to read. Style: candid documentary photograph of a real place, not an advertisement, not CGI, not a composite.
